sights.n: Noboribetsu Bear Park (のぼりべつクマ牧場)
sights.address: Noboribetsu Onsen-chō (ropeway from the onsen town), Noboribetsu, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: A 7-minute ropeway up Mt Shihorei to ~100 Ezo brown bears — with the 'human cage' where people, not bears, are behind the bars.

sights.n: Sendai-han Shiraoi Moto-Jin'ya Site & Museum (仙台藩白老元陣屋跡・資料館)
sights.address: Jin'ya-chō, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: 1856 coastal-defence camp of the Sendai domain — a national historic site with earthworks in a 66,000 m² park and a museum of ~300 objects.
Said founded in 826 and named one of the shogunate's three official Ezo temples (1804) — a national historic site, Hokkaido Heritage, and a cherry 'flower temple' with its rock-splitting sakura.

sights.n: Mt Sokuryō Observatory, Muroran (測量山展望台)
sights.w: A 200 m hill named for the Meiji surveyors who planned the Sapporo road — 360° views over the port, Hakuchō Bridge and the steelworks; a Japan Night View Heritage site.

sights.n: Hokkaido Museum of Northern Peoples, Abashiri (北海道立北方民族博物館)
sights.address: Mt Tento, Shiomi, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Japan's only museum of the circumpolar peoples — Ainu, Okhotsk culture, Inuit, Sámi — on Mt Tento near the drift-ice museum.

sights.n: Moyoro Shell Mound & Site Museum, Abashiri (モヨロ貝塚・モヨロ貝塚館)
sights.address: Mouth of the Abashiri River, Kitamachi, Abashiri, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: National historic site of the seafaring Okhotsk culture (5th–9th c.) at the Abashiri river mouth, with burials, shell middens and a site museum.

sights.n: Hosooka Observatory, Kushiro Marsh (細岡展望台)
sights.address: Tōro, Kushiro-chō, Kushiro District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: The 'Taikanbō' — the classic view of the marsh with the Kushiro River's S-bends to the horizon and the Akan peaks behind; famed at sunset.

sights.n: Cape Kiritappu (霧多布岬 / 湯沸岬)
sights.address: Tōbutsu, Hamanaka, Akkeshi District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Sheer cliffs on the Pacific where sea otters and seals are watched from the headland — Hamanaka's signature viewpoint.

sights.n: Akan International Crane Center 'GRUS' (阿寒国際ツルセンター)
sights.w: Winter feeding ground and research centre where red-crowned cranes dance on the snowfields at close range.
40–50 m sea cliffs jutting into the Okhotsk with a lone lighthouse — a drift-ice lookout from late January to early March.

sights.n: Meiji Park & Brick Silos, Nemuro (明治公園)
sights.w: Site of Hokkaido's second state ranch (1875); its three 15 m red-brick silos are among Japan's largest — registered cultural property and modernization heritage.

sights.address: Between Lake Fūren and Nemuro Bay, Nemuro, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: An 8 km sandspit with a rare pure forest of Sakhalin spruce on dunes, 3 km of rugosa roses and some of Hokkaido's best birding.

sights.n: Michi-no-eki Nakasatsunai & Bean Museum (道の駅 なかさつない)
sights.w: Flower-filled roadside station under the Hidaka range with seven eateries, a bean museum and a pioneer memorial hall — the gateway to the Nakasatsunai art village.

sights.n: Shichiku Garden, Obihiro (紫竹ガーデン)
sights.w: Shichiku Akiyo's 18,000-tsubo flower garden on the Tokachi plain — ~2,500 varieties and a fixture of the Hokkaido Garden Path.

sights.n: Former Aikoku Station, Obihiro (旧国鉄広尾線 愛国駅)
sights.w: The 'From Aikoku (Land of Love) to Kōfuku (Happiness)' ticket station of the closed Hiroo Line — now a small railway museum with an SL.

sights.n: Wakkanai Fukukō Market (稚内副港市場)
sights.w: Harbourside complex of seafood market, Hatoba Yokochō food stalls, the Minato no Yu onsen with sea views and a Karafuto history exhibit.

sights.n: Otatomari Pond, Rishiri (オタトマリ沼)
sights.address: Numaura, Oniwaki, Rishirifuji, Rishiri District, Hokkaido, Japan
sights.w: Rishiri's largest pond, ringed by Japan's northernmost Sakhalin-spruce forest, with Mt Rishiri reflected in still water.
